extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from XML results, figures, Table 3 leakage, Supplementary Figure S2 text, and NMR methods/results.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Peptide length determines antimicrobial, hemolytic, and vesicle-leakage activity through hydrophobic matching with the membrane core; peptides below the threshold remain weak or inactive while longer peptides can permeabilize membranes.
mechanism_claims.limitations: The exact threshold differs by organism and lipid system; database-only extra organisms in CAMP/dbAMP are not promoted to primary-paper evidence.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: KIA peptides in DMPC oriented membrane samples
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Solid-state NMR supports length-dependent orientation changes: shorter KIA14/KIA15 are surface-bound, KIA17/KIA19 adopt inserted or tilted states, and the longest peptides perturb the bilayer.
mechanism_claims.limitations: NMR was performed in a DMPC model membrane and should not be read as a direct measurement in every bacterial or erythrocyte membrane.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: membrane permeabilization model for KIA peptides
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper proposes transmembrane pore formation when peptide length matches bilayer thickness, while explicitly leaving barrel-stave versus toroidal pore geometry unresolved.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Figure 3 is a schematic; pore geometry is not normalized into a single database mechanism label.
